## Further Reading

Datar, S. M., & Rajan, M. V. (2021). *Horngren's cost accounting: A managerial emphasis* (17th ed.). Pearson. <https://www.pearson.com/en-us/pearsonplus/p/9780136713845> The standard cost accounting text. Its chapters on cost-volume-profit analysis, on flexible budgets and sales-volume variances, and on estimating cost behavior with regression develop the managerial accounting behind this chapter's models in depth.

Frontline Systems. (n.d.). *Excel Solver: Create Solver reports*. <https://www.solver.com/excel-solver-create-solver-reports> The developer of Excel's Solver explains the Answer, Sensitivity, and Limits reports and when each is available. Its related pages explain how to read the shadow prices and reduced costs in the Sensitivity report.

Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). *Forecasting: Principles and practice* (3rd ed.). OTexts. <https://otexts.com/fpp3/> A free, widely used online textbook on forecasting. Its chapters on simple benchmark methods and on evaluating forecast accuracy expand on the backtesting approach of Tutorial 7.1, and later chapters cover methods for seasonal and trending series.

Microsoft. (2026c). *Introduction to What-If Analysis*. Microsoft Support. <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/introduction-to-what-if-analysis> Microsoft's overview of Scenario Manager, Goal Seek, and data tables, with links to step-by-step instructions for each tool and to Solver.

Nikitkov, A. (2024). Budget variance analysis case: Contrasting Excel with Tableau. *Accounting Perspectives*, *23*(4), 605–612. <https://doi.org/10.1111/1911-3838.12383> A teaching case in which you prepare a budgetary variance analysis for a board meeting, first in Excel and then as a visual analysis in Tableau. It extends the variance report of Tutorial 7.2 toward the presentation tools of Part IV.

Silvester, K. J. (2017). Faith's Country Primitives: An Excel project in flexible budgeting and standard cost analysis. *Journal of Business Case Studies*, *13*(4), 85–98. <https://doi.org/10.19030/jbcs.v13i4.10030> An Excel case project that takes you through budgeting, flexible budgets, and standard cost variances in one integrated exercise, so that you can see how the individual variance calculations fit together.

Yahya-Zadeh, M. (2002). A linear programming framework for flexible budgeting and its application to classroom teaching. *Issues in Accounting Education*, *17*(1), 69–93. <https://doi.org/10.2308/iace.2002.17.1.69> An article that builds production and market constraints into flexible budgeting and variance analysis with linear programming. It connects the flexible budget of Tutorial 7.2 with the Solver model of Exercise 7.4.
